al-Shahrastānī, al-Milal, p. 49 (2nd ed., Cairo). By the final position mentioned here, al-Shahrastānī means the position of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī. Aḥmad Amīn, however, also regards this final position as a form of determinism, contrary to al-Shahrastānī. Amīn argues that the doctrine of kasb (“acquisition”) changes nothing in substance and is simply a new way of expressing determinism. According to this doctrine, a created human power has no effect on the act that occurs, while the act called “acquisition” is still created by God. Why go in circles, Amīn asks, when the conclusion is still determinism? See Aḥmad Amīn, Ḍuḥā al-Islām, vol. 2, p. 57.↩︎
